name: Dororo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 1975. The East Papuan Phylum in general. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1 (PL C-38), 783-804.
sources.note: p. 787: Kazukuru Family = Kazukuru, Guliguli, Dororo (extinct). Classification only.

sources.citation: Voegelin, C. F. & F. M. Voegelin. 1965. Languages of the World: Indo-Pacific fascicle five. Anthropological Linguistics 7(9).
sources.note: 'Guliguli and Dororo, both of which appear to be so closely related to Kazukuru that all three may be dialects of one language.' Classification only.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request 2019-021: adopted merge [drr] Dororo into [kzk] Kazukuru (2020-01-23). SIL International.
sources.note: pp. 2-3: merge rationale (Hammarstrom 2015; 'a 19-item wordlist purportedly from Dororo shows 79% cognacy with Kazukuru'; Davis 2003 found no memory of the name). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Dunn, Michael & Malcolm Ross. 2007. Is Kazukuru really non-Austronesian? Oceanic Linguistics 46(1): 210-231. doi:10.1353/ol.2007.0018
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 (pp. 216-218) reproduces the 19 Dororo forms of Lanyon-Orgill 1953 in Table 1 (p. 217) and calls Dororo and Guliguli 'transcription variants of Kazukuru rather than distinct dialects'; Sec. 4.1 Phonology (pp. 218-219) treats only Kazukuru graphemes, prenasalized voiced stops, five vowels, (C)V syllables, r/l. Nothing on stress, accent or prosody anywhere. SILENT.

sources.citation: Davis, Karen. 2003. A grammar of the Hoava language, Western Solomons. Pacific Linguistics 535. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open repository, handle 1885/146158)
sources.note: p. 15: 'Two related dialects of Kazukuru are said to have been spoken on the slopes of Mount Vina Roni... The names of the dialects are given as Dororo and Guliguli, but there was no one in present day Kusaghe who had heard of them, and Lanyon-Orgill does not identify his informant.' Its phonology chapter is Hoava only; nothing on Dororo stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-72.
sources.note: Kazukuru 'was reported to have two dialects or sublanguages, Doriri and Guliguli (Lanyon-Orgill 1953)'; index 'Dororo* see KAZUKURU*'. Name only; no data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Languoid page doro1267 (Bookkeeping: Dororo) and reference record 127838 (Lanyon-Orgill 1953).
sources.note: Retired entry; three refs only (Dunn & Ross 2007, Lanyon-Orgill 1953 [hhtype overview;comparative;wordlist, no URL], ISO CR 2019-021); 0 descriptive references. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Waterhouse, J. H. L. & S. H. Ray. 1931. The Kazukuru language of New Georgia. Man 31: 123-126.
sources.note: Kazukuru proper only (does not mention Dororo); sole phonological remark is that sounds are 'written as in Roviana'; no accent marks, no stress statement.
'Some additional Kazukuru data and the only information on Dororo and Guliguli (two short wordlists) were published by Peter Lanyon-Orgill in 1953.' No phonology or stress information.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2011. On the margins of Pacific linguistics: P. A. Lanyon-Orgill. Language & History 54(2): 164-177.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Assesses the reliability of Lanyon-Orgill's data, relevant to whether the Dororo list is genuine; not a description and will not contain a stress rule.

sources.citation: Lanyon-Orgill, Peter A. 1953. The Papuan languages of the New Georgian Archipelago, Solomon Islands. Journal of Austronesian Studies 1(1): 122-138.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only primary record of Dororo (19-word list); would show whether Lanyon-Orgill marked accent or commented on it (unlikely: Dunn & Ross reproduce the forms unaccented and flag reliability problems).
